Respiratory cancers in carriers were concentrated in ever-smokers.
The tobacco-related cancers in carriers, including head and neck carcinoma, occurred mainly in ever-smokers.

edges.description: UV exposure raises melanoma penetrance on the CDKN2A carrier background.

nodes.description: Some carriers have a high total nevus count with clinically atypical nevi, but the extent varies considerably. In Swedish carriers, one or more clinically atypical nevi correlated with carrier status while total nevus counts were low and no participant met atypical mole syndrome criteria.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Some affected individuals have a high total nevus count (often >50 nevi) and atypical-appearing nevi, although the number and extent of atypical nevi can vary significantly.

evidence.reference_title: Swedish CDKN2A mutation carriers do not present the atypical mole syndrome phenotype.
evidence.snippet: No participant fulfilled the atypical mole syndrome phenotype criteria.

nodes.description: Avoidance of ultraviolet light, particularly sunburns and tanning booths.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Ultraviolet light exposure, particularly sunburns and tanning booths; tobacco use.

meta.association: Heterozygous germline loss-of-function variants in CDKN2A cause melanoma-pancreatic cancer syndrome; pancreatic cancer risk is associated with variants that affect p16INK4A.

evidence.reference_title: A novel CDKN2A in-frame deletion associated with pancreatic cancer-melanoma syndrome.
evidence.snippet: About 30% of PCMS cases carry mutations in CDKN2A.

evidence.reference_title: FAMMM syndrome: pathogenesis and management.
evidence.snippet: Across multiple studies, germline mutations in the INK4a antioncogene encoding p16 protein were found on average in approximately 40% of the FAMMM syndrome.

nodes.description: Cutaneous malignant melanoma, often multiple primaries and earlier in life than sporadic melanoma; median age at diagnosis was 36 years among Swedish p.Arg112dup carriers. Lifetime risk is strongly ascertainment-dependent (see inheritance), so no single frequency band is given.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: CDKN2A cancer predisposition is characterized by an increased risk of developing multiple cutaneous melanomas, pancreatic cancer, and other tumors including gliomas and astrocytomas.

evidence.reference_title: Melanoma genetics: a review of genetic factors and clinical phenotypes in familial melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Familial melanoma patients develop melanomas earlier and are prone to developing multiple primary melanomas.

evidence.reference_title: Swedish CDKN2A mutation carriers do not present the atypical mole syndrome phenotype.
evidence.snippet: 29 invasive melanomas in 16 patients were recorded, all in the 38 verified CDKN2A mutation carriers. Median age at diagnosis was 36 years.

nodes.description: Unopposed MDM2 ubiquitinates p53 and targets it for proteasomal degradation.

evidence.reference_title: Regulatory Network of ARF in Cancer Development.
evidence.snippet: As a factor that induces senescence, the role of ARF as a tumor suppressor is closely linked to the p53-MDM2 axis, which is a key process that restrains tumor formation.

nodes.description: With the p16INK4A-RB brake lost, melanocytes held in oncogene-induced senescence in nevi can bypass that arrest and expand clonally toward melanoma. Whether the same senescence bypass is the operative step in the pancreatic duct is inferred from the shared p16-RB mechanism rather than shown in carrier tissue.
nodes.id: Escape from Cellular Senescence and Clonal Expansion

evidence.reference_title: Genome-Wide Overexpression Screen Identifies Genes Able to Bypass p16-Mediated Senescence in Melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Malignant melanomas often arise from nevi, which result from initial oncogene-induced hyperproliferation of melanocytes that are maintained in a CDKN2A/p16-mediated senescent state.

evidence.reference_title: Cooperative effects of INK4a and ras in melanoma susceptibility in vivo.
evidence.snippet: These results show that loss of ink4a and activation of Ras can cooperate to accelerate the development of melanoma

nodes.description: The constitutional first hit: a heterozygous germline loss-of-function variant in CDKN2A, carried by every somatic cell. Founder alleles include the Dutch p16-Leiden 19-bp exon 2 deletion (c.225_243del) and the Swedish p.Arg112dup; in-frame deletions and missense variants that impair p16INK4A folding and CDK4 binding are also reported. Exon 2 variants can also alter the overlapping p14ARF reading frame.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of CDKN2A cancer predisposition is established in a proband by identification of a heterozygous germline pathogenic variant in CDKN2A by molecular genetic testing.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of developing pancreatic cancer in families with familial atypical multiple mole melanoma associated with a specific 19 deletion of p16 (p16-Leiden).
evidence.snippet: A p16-Leiden mutation was identified in 19 families. These families included 86 patients with melanoma. The second most frequent cancer was pancreatic cancer, which was observed in 15 patients from 7 families.

evidence.reference_title: A novel CDKN2A in-frame deletion associated with pancreatic cancer-melanoma syndrome.
evidence.snippet: By segregation analysis, the c.52_57delACGGCC was proven to segregate in kindred with cutaneous melanoma (CM), in kindred with CM and pancreatic cancer, and in a single case presenting only with pancreatic cancer.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous germline CDKN2A pathogenic variants; the pancreatic cancer risk is associated with variants that affect the p16INK4A protein.

nodes.description: Head and neck carcinomas are among the tobacco-related cancers at elevated risk in p.Arg112dup carriers and their relatives.
nodes.id: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

evidence.reference_title: High risk of tobacco-related cancers in CDKN2A mutation-positive melanoma families.
evidence.snippet: CDKN2A p.Arg112dup mutation carriers from melanoma-prone families and their FDRs and SDRs have elevated risk for pancreatic, lung, head and neck and gastro-oesophageal carcinomas.

nodes.description: Melanocyte-specific expression of activated H-ras on an Ink4a-deficient background produces spontaneous cutaneous melanoma with short latency and high penetrance, with loss of the wild-type Ink4a allele in tumors from heterozygous mice. The model addresses the melanoma arm only.
nodes.id: Ink4a-deficient mice with melanocyte-specific activated H-ras

evidence.reference_title: Cooperative effects of INK4a and ras in melanoma susceptibility in vivo.
evidence.snippet: mice with melanocyte-specific expression of activated H-rasG12V on an ink4a-deficient background develop spontaneous cutaneous melanomas after a short latency and with high penetrance

nodes.description: p14ARF, encoded from exon 1beta and an alternative reading frame of exon 2, sequesters MDM2. Many exon 2 variants affect both proteins. ARF haploinsufficiency has been associated with melanoma predisposition, but in the Dutch series variants affecting only p14ARF were not associated with pancreatic cancer, so this arm is not linked to the pancreatic phenotype here.

evidence.reference_title: INK4a/ARF: a multifunctional tumor suppressor locus.
evidence.snippet: The INK4a/ARF locus encodes two physically linked tumor suppressor proteins, p16(INK4a) and ARF, which regulate the RB and p53 pathways, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Germline mutation of ARF in a melanoma kindred.
evidence.snippet: Overall, the data suggest a direct role for ARF haploinsufficiency in melanoma predisposition and co-operation between ARF and CDKN2A in tumour formation

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations for pancreatic cancer risk in Dutch melanoma families with pathogenic CDKN2A variants.
evidence.snippet: There is no clinical evidence that impairment of only the p14ARF protein leads to an increased PDAC risk.

nodes.description: p16INK4A binds CDK4 and CDK6 and blocks their activation by cyclin D. Pathogenic variants destabilize the protein or abolish its binding partners. Loss of p16INK4A is the arm of the locus that carries the pancreatic cancer risk.

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: The p16INK4a tumor suppressor protein functions as an inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6, the D-type cyclin-dependent kinases that initiate the phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor protein, RB.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations for pancreatic cancer risk in Dutch melanoma families with pathogenic CDKN2A variants.
evidence.snippet: PDAC developed in 95 of 163 families (58%, including 373 of 629 proven carriers) harbouring a variant with an effect on the p16INK4a protein, whereas PDAC did not occur in the 9 families (20 proven carriers) with a variant affecting only p14ARF.

evidence.reference_title: A novel CDKN2A in-frame deletion associated with pancreatic cancer-melanoma syndrome.
evidence.snippet: A computational approach for studying the effect of mutational changes over p16 protein structure showed that both the deletion and the duplication of the c.52_57 nucleotides result in protein misfolding and loss of interactors' binding.

evidence.reference_title: Structural consequences of tumor-derived mutations in p16INK4a probed by limited proteolysis.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that the N-terminal half of p16 is significantly more sensitive to proteolysis in both tumor-derived mutant proteins than in the wild type, suggesting that this region is particularly unstable.

nodes.description: Carriers of the Swedish p.Arg112dup founder variant had an elevated risk of respiratory cancers, seen mainly in ever-smokers.

evidence.reference_title: High risk of tobacco-related cancers in CDKN2A mutation-positive melanoma families.
evidence.snippet: In carriers prospective RR for non-melanoma cancers was 5.0 (95% CI 3.7 to 7.3), for pancreatic cancer 43.8 (95% CI 13.8 to 139.0), for cancers in upper digestive tissues 17.1 (95% CI 6.3 to 46.5), and in respiratory tissues 15.6 (5.4 to 46.0).

nodes.description: Dermatologic examination for melanoma every six months with monthly self-skin examination for carriers. At-risk relatives whose genetic status is unknown, including children, should have skin examinations at well-child or health maintenance visits.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Dermatologic examination for melanoma every six months; monthly self-skin examinations

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: At-risk family members whose genetic status is unknown should undergo skin exams at their well child / health maintenance visits.

nodes.description: Annual surveillance alternating MRCP and endoscopic ultrasound from age 40 years, or 10 years younger than the earliest exocrine pancreatic cancer in the family if earlier. The CAPS Consortium recommends surveillance for CDKN2A carriers from age 40 irrespective of family history of pancreatic cancer. In the Leiden program (annual MRI with optional EUS), most screen-detected PDACs were resectable and surveillance was cost-effective.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: annual alternating magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography and endoscopic ultrasound starting at age 40 years or 10 years younger than the earliest exocrine pancreatic cancer diagnosis in the family, whichever is earlier

evidence.reference_title: Management of patients with increased risk for familial pancreatic cancer: updated recommendations from the International Cancer of the Pancreas Screening (CAPS) Consortium.
evidence.snippet: Surveillance for CDKN2A and STK11 (Peutz-Jegher syndrome) mutation carriers is recommended irrespective of patients’ family history of pancreatic cancer, because of their high lifetime risk.

evidence.reference_title: Management of patients with increased risk for familial pancreatic cancer: updated recommendations from the International Cancer of the Pancreas Screening (CAPS) Consortium.
evidence.snippet: surveillance from age 40 is recommended for CDKN2A mutation carriers

evidence.reference_title: Cost-effectiveness of pancreas surveillance: The CDKN2A-p16-Leiden cohort.
evidence.snippet: A total of 347 mutation carriers participated in the surveillance program. PDAC was detected in 31 patients (8.9%) and the tumor could be resected in 22 patients (71.0%). Long-term cure among patients with resected PDAC was estimated at 47.1% (p < 0.001).

nodes.description: Pancreatic carcinoma, conventional ductal adenocarcinoma in nearly all studied cases, at a mean age of 58 years (range 38-77) in Dutch p16-Leiden families; cumulative risk to age 75 was 17% in putative p16-Leiden carriers and 19% in c.67G>C carriers. The risk is associated with variants affecting p16INK4A.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of developing pancreatic cancer in families with familial atypical multiple mole melanoma associated with a specific 19 deletion of p16 (p16-Leiden).
evidence.snippet: The mean age at diagnosis of pancreatic cancer was 58 years (range 38-77 years). The estimated cumulative risk of developing pancreatic cancer in putative mutation carriers by age 75 years was 17%.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations for pancreatic cancer risk in Dutch melanoma families with pathogenic CDKN2A variants.
evidence.snippet: The standardised incidence ratio was 19.1 (95% CI 8.3 to 33.6) and the cumulative PDAC incidence at age 75 years (lifetime risk) was 19% (95% CI 7.5% to 30.1%).

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic carcinoma in carriers of a specific 19 base pair deletion of CDKN2A/p16 (p16-leiden).
evidence.snippet: Histology was considered as conventional ductal adenocarcinoma in 11 of 12 and neuroendocrine carcinoma (1 of 12).

nodes.description: Hyperphosphorylated RB releases E2F, driving the G1-to-S transition independently of normal mitogenic control.
nodes.id: RB Inactivation and Unchecked G1/S Transition

biological_processes: negative regulation of G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: Thus, p16INK4a has the capacity to arrest cells in the G1-phase of the cell cycle and its probable physiological role is in the implementation of irreversible growth arrest termed cellular senescence.

nodes.description: Surgical resection of surveillance-detected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the only route to cure; otherwise standard tumor-specific treatment applies to melanoma and pancreatic cancer.

evidence.reference_title: Cost-effectiveness of pancreas surveillance: The CDKN2A-p16-Leiden cohort.
evidence.snippet: The tumor could be resected in most patients with a screen-detected PDAC. These patients had considerably better survival and as a result annual surveillance was found to be cost-effective.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Standard treatment for melanoma, pancreatic cancer, and other cancers.

nodes.description: In pancreatic carcinomas from p16-Leiden carriers, KRAS codon 12 mutations were present in nearly all tumors and already in precursor lesions, in one case before loss of p16 expression; TP53 mutation and SMAD4 loss were present in a subset. These are the cooperating somatic lesions through which a carrier's pancreatic ductal epithelium progresses to conventional ductal adenocarcinoma.
nodes.id: Somatic KRAS Activation in Pancreatic Precursor Lesions

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic carcinoma in carriers of a specific 19 base pair deletion of CDKN2A/p16 (p16-leiden).
evidence.snippet: K-ras codon 12 mutations were present in 9 of 10 and in three precursor lesions even before abrogation of p16 protein expression was seen (one of three).

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic carcinoma in carriers of a specific 19 base pair deletion of CDKN2A/p16 (p16-leiden).
evidence.snippet: The p16-Leiden deletion was associated with progression toward conventional ductal adenocarcinomas in all cases but one.

genetic_context.description: Somatic activating KRAS codon 12 mutation in pancreatic precursor lesions and carcinoma.

nodes.description: In the tumor, p16INK4A function is lost from the remaining allele. In pancreatic carcinomas from p16-Leiden carriers, p16 immunostaining was absent in every tumor tested, but loss of heterozygosity of the wild-type allele was demonstrated in only 2 of 7, so the mechanism of second-allele inactivation is not established for most pancreatic tumors (promoter methylation and intragenic mutation were not reported in the cited study). In melanoma, consistent loss of the wild-type allele is seen in the Ink4a-heterozygous mouse model, and somatic inactivation of the wild-type allele has been documented in a human melanoma from a germline ARF-variant kindred.

animal_models.genotype: Melanocyte-specific H-rasG12V transgene on an ink4a-null or ink4a-heterozygous background
animal_models.name: Ink4a-deficient mice with melanocyte-specific activated H-ras

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic carcinoma in carriers of a specific 19 base pair deletion of CDKN2A/p16 (p16-leiden).
evidence.snippet: Loss of heterozygosity of the wild-type allele was present in 2 of 7 tumors analyzed. Immunostaining for p16 was negative in 10 of 10.

evidence.reference_title: Germline mutation of ARF in a melanoma kindred.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the melanoma from one individual revealed a 62 bp deletion in exon 3 of the wildtype allele and loss of the mutant allele; these somatic changes would affect both CDKN2A and ARF.

evidence.reference_title: Cooperative effects of INK4a and ras in melanoma susceptibility in vivo.
evidence.snippet: Consistent loss of the wild-type ink4a allele was observed in tumors arising in ink4a heterozygous transgenic mice.

genetic_context.description: Somatic loss of the wild-type CDKN2A allele (loss of heterozygosity, deletion or intragenic mutation) on the germline background.

nodes.description: Carriers should abstain from tobacco, given the strong interaction between smoking and pancreatic, respiratory and upper digestive cancer risk.

evidence.reference_title: High risk of tobacco-related cancers in CDKN2A mutation-positive melanoma families.
evidence.snippet: CDKN2A mutation carriers should be counselled to abstain from smoking.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Ultraviolet light exposure, particularly sunburns and tanning booths; tobacco use.

nodes.description: Tobacco smoking amplifies the risk of pancreatic, respiratory and upper digestive cancers in carriers, a gene-environment interaction that is the basis for counselling carriers to abstain from smoking.

evidence.reference_title: High risk of tobacco-related cancers in CDKN2A mutation-positive melanoma families.
evidence.snippet: CDKN2A mutation carriers should be counselled to abstain from smoking.

nodes.description: Ultraviolet exposure modifies melanoma penetrance across geographic latitude, although studies conflict on which patterns of sun exposure, including childhood and adolescent exposure, raise risk in familial melanoma.

evidence.reference_title: Melanoma genetics: a review of genetic factors and clinical phenotypes in familial melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Yet cumulative studies are conflicting on whether ultraviolet radiation, including sunburns, early childhood and adolescent sun exposure, and chronic exposure, increases melanoma risk in familial melanoma.

nodes.description: Without p16INK4A, CDK4/6-cyclin D complexes are constitutively active and phosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein. The same state is reached by INK4-insensitive CDK4 variants in the CDK4 hereditary melanoma genocopy.

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: The p16INK4a tumor suppressor protein functions as an inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6, the D-type cyclin-dependent kinases that initiate the phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor protein, RB.

evidence.reference_title: Wide spectrum of tumors in knock-in mice carrying a Cdk4 protein insensitive to INK4 inhibitors.
evidence.snippet: This mutation (replacement of Arg24 by Cys) was first found in patients with hereditary melanoma and renders Cdk4 insensitive to INK4 inhibitors.

nodes.description: Dutch founder 19-bp deletion in exon 2 that inactivates p16INK4A; the most prevalent pathogenic CDKN2A variant in the Dutch national familial melanoma database.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlations for pancreatic cancer risk in Dutch melanoma families with pathogenic CDKN2A variants.
evidence.snippet: The most prevalent variant was the founder mutation c.225_243del (p16-Leiden, 484 proven carriers).

nodes.description: Swedish founder in-frame duplication in exon 2 of CDKN2A, associated with a broad tobacco-related cancer spectrum in carriers.

evidence.reference_title: High risk of tobacco-related cancers in CDKN2A mutation-positive melanoma families.
evidence.snippet: A single founder mutation, p.Arg112dup, accounts for the majority of CDKN2A mutations in Swedish carriers.
